# iTunesDB golden fixtures

`original-empty.b64` is the Base64 representation of a 3,508-byte iTunesDB
generated by the Original iOpenPod `write_mhbd` implementation with no tracks,
fixed database and master-playlist IDs, Unix time 1,700,000,000, and random seed 0.
It was imported on 2026-08-27 as the local compatibility baseline described by
ADR-0004.

Decoded SHA-256:
`23576f070e32bd561f803724a98606ed8ce95543b30917819565031b57bff33b`.

The encoded text form keeps the fixture reviewable and platform-neutral. Tests
decode it strictly before asserting complete byte equality.

## Captured album index, sort type 36

`captured-album-index-36.b64` is an anonymized 69,884-byte reconstruction of sorting
evidence from the historical 20,138,994-byte captured database. It contains 60 Tracks
across nine complete native album groups, their representatives, and both Master
Playlists. The earlier reduced fixture was replaced on 2026-10-08 with fresh unsigned
Chunks, fabricated names, and synthetic Track, album, Playlist, and persistent IDs.
Only album membership, representative relationships, sort-field presence, compilation
flags, disc/track numbers, and captured relative ordering remain. Artist/album labels
preserve every pairwise album comparison under all supported collation profiles,
including the punctuation-sensitive pair. Member sort disagreements remain distinct.

`captured-album-index-36.json` records source and fixture SHA-256 hashes, synthetic
fixture Track IDs, and the captured order translated to those synthetic IDs. No
original-to-synthetic identity mapping is stored. Expected sequences originate in
the original MHOD 52 records, not the index implementation under test.
The database alone supplies the test evidence, without a runtime dependency on
Original iOpenPod or the user's capture folder.

See [sort-36 research](../../../docs/research/itunesdb-sort-36.md) for the observed
rules and evidence limits.

## Captured sort overrides, empty albums, and compilation placement

`captured-album-index-36-overrides.b64` is an anonymized 10,720-byte fixture from
the 1,203,015-byte database supplied with a sort-36 failure on 2026-10-08. Seven
selected Tracks preserve their original album representatives' sorting relationships:
field presence, compilation flags, disc/track numbers, album ownership, and
representative references. Names and identifiers are fabricated, including the
article-sensitive artist `The Zeta` and its neighbor `Thistle`. Both Master sequences
and their sort-36 orders are filtered from the original, then remapped to reduced
positions and synthetic identities.
Zero representative references remain zero; their selected member is the original
disc/track fallback in retained sort-36 order.

Both fixtures use fresh headers and neutral Track/Library labels; media types are
normalized to audio. Account information, media paths, timestamps, podcast metadata,
artwork, other indexes, Unknown Data, and copied padding are omitted. They are sorting
evidence in reconstructed layouts, not lossless excerpts or publishable device
databases. Their manifests record source and fixture hashes and the captured order
using synthetic IDs. See [fixture privacy](../README.md) and the automated checks
in `tests/test_fixture_privacy.py`.

## Nano 6 HASHAB signature envelopes

`nano6-hashab-envelopes.json` reconstructs the signing convention established by
two Apple-written Nano 6 CDB captures investigated on 2026-10-22. The original
files and their device GUID remain private and are not stored in the repository.
The source SHA-256 values identify the evidence without including its contents.

Each stored database is a fresh 277-byte compressed example containing only an
empty Track dataset, synthetic database IDs, and the fabricated GUID
`0123456789abcdef`. Only the 23 random envelope bytes from each Apple signature
are retained. Names, media, dates, device identities, private Chunks, unknown
payloads, and copied padding are omitted. An allowlist test reconstructs every
database byte outside the signature from fresh Chunks.

Expected 57-byte signatures were generated separately from the production signer
using the pinned upstream `dstaley/hashab` implementation at commit
`f80d46432204c6238cad7d8ca3b3dd52ea66836b`, whose reconstruction was first checked
against both complete Apple captures. The fixture includes the correct scheme-3
envelope, the former deterministic scheme-4 envelope published under scheme 3, both
normalized digests, and the expected deterministic scheme-3 signing result.
These are synthetic regressions derived from captured behavior, not untouched
Apple output or databases intended for a physical device.

`tests/iPodDB/iTunesDB/test_hashab_captures.py` also offers read-only tests against
the four private captures when `IOPENPOD_NANO6_CAPTURES` names their parent folder.
That folder must contain `fresh apple`, `apple`, `v1 bad ig`, and `v2 bad`; the
device GUID is read from the last folder's SysInfo. These opt-in tests verify both
actual Apple CDBs, reject both original incorrect iOpenPod signatures, match the
independently prepared signature-only repair hash, and verify all four Locations
Checksum Books. Without the environment variable only these private-data tests
skip; the synthetic regressions run everywhere.
